newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOBSLEIGH-ACUPUNCTURIST HELPS U.S. TO WORLD CUP WIN.
newsitem.headline: BOBSLEIGH-ACUPUNCTURIST HELPS U.S. TO WORLD CUP WIN.

text.p: A Japanese acupuncturist and an American medical team helped Brian Shimer pilot USA I to its first four-man World Cup bobsleigh victory of the season on Tuesday.
USA I, which led after the first run, was edged by Dirk Wieses' Germany II by one-hundredth of a second on the second run, but earned the win with a combined time of one minute 45.75 seconds.
Wiese, eighth in the first run, finished .27 seconds behind, while Bruno Mongeons' France I was third overall, a further .05 seconds behind.
Shimer, who injured his back on Saturday while warming up for the second heat of the two-man event in which he placed fourth, could barely walk before the race.

"Our trainer and chiropractor worked on my back night and day for the last three days to try to get me ready for the race," said the 34-year-old former college running back. "I didn't think it was going to be possible.
"Normally, with my back like this, I wouldn't think about doing anything, let along driving a bobsled," said Shimer, who also visited an acupuncturist on race morning. "It was all or nothing."
His crew responded by producing the two fastest starts of the day, which provided Shimer with the margin he needed.
"We won this race at the start," he said. "My team really dug deep so I'm giving this race to them. All I had to do was have two clean trips. They weren't perfect but they were good enough."
Crew member Randy Jones said he knew Shimer would be able to push if he could walk.
"It was just a question of how hard he could push," Jones said. "When we saw the start times, we thought, 'we've got to kick him in the back tomorrow'."
Shimer, who started all four training heats sitting in the sled, faces another race on Wednesday, since Tuesday's event made up for a postponed World Cup race in Calgary last week.
